messages.author: 2a3a0c6a456f3043
messages.subject: Removal sampling with unmarkedFrameMPois example?
parts:
Hi,

Does anyone have a removal sampling example with observation level covariates? I'm trying to use multinomPois to analyze mammal kill trapping over a 4 day period where detection can vary daily as a function of trapping effort and other daily (observation-level) covariates. I'm having trouble even getting unmarkedFrameMPois to like the obsCovs input. It should be an RxJ (102 trap stations by 4 observations/station) matrix just like the count data (y). When I enter a single covariate with a dataframe with 102 x 4 dimensions, I get an error that obsCovs is the wrong size and should be equal to M*obsNum. I am not sure what the M is. I don't think M is listed in the documentation for unmarkedFrameMPois.

<pre><code>
Error in validObject(.Object) :
  invalid class “unmarkedFrame” object: obsCovData does not have M*obsNum rows.
</code></pre>

Here is an example

<pre><code>
data(ovendata)

obscovs = data.frame(matrix(data=rnorm(70*3, mean=0, sd=1), nrow=70, ncol=3))
names(obscovs) = names=c("d1", "d2", "d3")

ovenFrame <- unmarkedFrameMPois(ovendata.list$data, siteCovs=as.data.frame(scale(ovendata.list$covariates[,-1])), type = "removal") # Works

ovenFrame <- unmarkedFrameMPois(ovendata.list$data, siteCovs=as.data.frame(scale(ovendata.list$covariates[,-1])), obsCovs = obscovs, type = "removal") # Fails

</code></pre>


Thanks,
Dan

messages.author: 527d9b3ec7deff2d
messages.subject: Re: Removal sampling with unmarkedFrameMPois example?
parts:
You need to specify obscovs as a list.  Also, in your example the data matrix is 70 x 4 (thus obscovs needs to match this). This here works:

data(ovendata)
obscovs = data.frame(matrix(data=rnorm(70*4, mean=0, sd=1), nrow=70, ncol=4))
ovenFrame <- unmarkedFrameMPois(ovendata.list$data, siteCovs=as.data.frame(scale(ovendata.list$covariates[,-1])), obsCovs = list(obscovs=obscovs), type = "removal")

And M is referring to the number of sites in the documentation for a regular unmarkedFrame.  Given the purposes here, it should be the same.

Thanks
Dan

messages.author: 985e455b8390aae3
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Re: Removal sampling with unmarkedFrameMPois example?
parts:
Daniel, I went through the same situation a few months ago.  Yes, the manual does seem to have some inconsistency of R*J vs. M*Obs.  I did end up having to make a named list.  As I had uneven sampling occasions, I had lots of NA.  Basically, I made a R*J matrix of NAs for every observation covariate, then overwrote NAs for where i did have data (uneven number of sampling efforts per site) leaving NAs for Js where there was no sampling (at the end of each site row).  Once this matrix was created for each obscov, I collected them in a named list and fed that list to the umf.

I've created a pared-down version of the code here...I hope you can follow it:

###  DATA MATRIX PREP
R <- length(sitelist)    # Number of sites
J <- max   (obsnum)      # Maximum number of observations per site

###  CREATE Y DATA MATRIX
y<-matrix(NA, R, J)
for(i in 1:R){
  count<-length(which(d$site==site[i]))     # count number of obs in current site
  y[i,1:count]<-d$y[d$site==site[i]]        # copy counts to matrix
}

###  CREATE OBSERVATION COVARIATE DATA FRAMES
obs<-data.frame(matrix(NA, R, J))     # Data frame for observer code
min<-data.frame(matrix(NA, R, J))     # ...number of minutes of search
rpast<-data.frame(matrix(NA, R, J))   # ...rain past
rnow<-data.frame(matrix(NA, R, J))    # ...rain now
# ...other observation covariates followed here

for(i in 1:R){
  count<-length(which(d$site==site[i]))     # count number of observations at current site
  obs[i,1:count]<-d$obs[d$site==site[i]]    # copy observer codes to dataframe
  min[i,1:count]<-as.numeric(d$minstd[d$site==site[i]]) # copy search duration (minutes) to dataframe
  rpast[i,1:count]<-as.factor(d$rpast[d$site==site[i]]) # copy rain code to datafram  
  rnow[i,1:count]<-as.factor(d$rnow[d$site==site[i]])   # copy observer codes to dataframe
  # ... same process for other obscovs here
}

##  COMBINE INTO OBERVATION COVARIATES LIST
obscov<-list(obs, min, rpast, rnow)   #create list
names(obscov)<-c("obs", "min", "rpast", "rnow")   # Name the list

##  CREAT UNMARKED MPOIS FRAME
umf<-unmarkedFrameMPois(y=y, siteCovs=scov, obsCovs=obscov, type="removal")
On Wed, Dec 4, 2013 at 9:13 AM, Daniel Hocking <dhoc...@unh.edu> wrote:

Oh, nevermind my last post. I now see that obsToY should be a 4 x 4 matrix and obsCovs needs to be a RxJ (same as M*obsNum). The documentation says that obsCovs can be a list of dataframes or just a dataframe, but it seems like it might have to be a list.

Thanks
Dan

On Wednesday, December 4, 2013 10:46:37 AM UTC-5, Dan Linden wrote:

And M is referring to the number of sites in the documentation for a regular unmarkedFrame.  Given the purposes here, it should be the same.
